title: Regular base change of the prime-power closed-immersion Gysin classes and the regular pinnings
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Work on small etale $D^+$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] with the roots-of-unity twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] between Noetherian regular affine schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme]; its ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence (each generator acts injectively modulo its predecessors), whose length is the locally constant codimension $c$. Write
$$\operatorname{Cl}_i:\Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c]\xrightarrow{\sim}i^!\Lambda_T$$
for the Gysin isomorphism of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] for $i$ (virtual relative dimension $d_i=-c$); for a closed immersion, the right adjoint $i^!$ of $Ri_!=i_*$ is the derived closed-support functor of [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel].

Regular base change. Let $r:T'\to T$ be a regular morphism with $T'$ a Noetherian affine scheme: $r$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and its fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre] remain regular after every finite extension of the residue field. Put $Z'=Z\times_TT'$, with $i':Z'\hookrightarrow T'$ and $r':Z'\to Z$. Then $T'$ and $Z'$ are regular, the ideal of $i'$ is locally generated by the pulled-back regular sequence, so $i'$ has codimension $c\circ r'$, and under the canonical exchange isomorphism $r'^*i^!\Lambda_T\xrightarrow{\sim}i'^!r^*\Lambda_T=i'^!\Lambda_{T'}$ of [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change], with $r'^*(\Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c])=\Lambda_{Z'}(-c\circ r')[-2c\circ r']$, one has $r'^*(\operatorname{Cl}_i)=\operatorname{Cl}_{i'}$.

Regular pinnings. If moreover $T$ is connected and excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], then for every $x\in T$, with $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,x}$ of codimension $\dim\mathcal O_{T,x}$, the canonical pinning of $\Lambda_T$ at $x$ in [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit] is $\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}^{-1}$, and the pinning of $\Lambda_T(m)[2m]$ at $x$ there is $\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}^{-1}(m)[2m]$.
